name: Church Government and Officers
path: Ecclesiology: The Doctrine of the Church

objectives.text: Identify Jesus Christ as the Head of the church who rules and cares for his people
Name the leaders Christ gives to his church, such as pastors, elders, and deacons
Describe how deacons in the early church cared for people in need
Practice praying in class for the pastors, elders, and deacons of a local church using what Scripture asks of members
Explain from Scripture why church leaders are called to be godly examples to the people they serve
Summarize the two ongoing offices of elder for oversight and deacon for service
Explain the character and ability qualifications Paul gives for elders and deacons
Describe how church officers are chosen, examined, and ordained according to the pattern in Acts and the Pastoral Epistles
Compare the responsibilities of elders in teaching and ruling with the responsibilities of deacons in mercy and service
Distinguish teaching elders who labor in preaching from ruling elders as the Reformed tradition reads 1 Timothy 5:17
Explain the biblical basis for members honoring and submitting to their elders along with the limit that obedience to God comes first
Explain how elders serve as under-shepherds who are accountable to Christ the Chief Shepherd
Analyze how Christ exercises his rule through the keys of the kingdom in preaching and church discipline
Distinguish the spiritual government of the church from the authority of the civil magistrate
Outline the steps of church discipline in Matthew 18 and the stages of admonition, suspension, and excommunication
Explain why the Reformed tradition holds that the public ministry of the Word requires gifted men who are lawfully called and approved
Explain the purposes of church discipline including restoration of the sinner, purity of the church, and the honor of Christ
Analyze the Jerusalem Council as a model for assemblies of elders deciding questions for the wider church
Analyze the New Testament use of the terms elder and overseer to explain the Reformed teaching of a plurality and parity of elders
Analyze how sessions, presbyteries, and assemblies relate and why their decisions bind only as far as they agree with Scripture
Evaluate episcopal, presbyterian, and congregational forms of church government against the teaching of Scripture
Evaluate the textual arguments for the Reformed tradition's position that the offices of pastor and elder are given to qualified men
Construct a reasoned case for a form of church government that answers objections from Scripture and church history
Compose a synthesis explaining how Christ rules his church as King through his Word, his officers, and his censures

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Christ as Head, officers, deacons, godly example, two offices, qualifications, elder and deacon roles, keys, discipline steps and purposes, lawful call, polity comparison, plurality, synthesis of Christ's rule). Changed the submission objective into an explanation of its basis and limits, and moved prayer for leaders to a classroom practice at grade 3. Added ordination and calling of officers, teaching versus ruling elders, under-shepherd accountability, church versus civil government, the Jerusalem Council and graded church courts, and the limits of synod authority. Replaced the vague 'connect' and 'interpret' items with specific objectives and anchored discipline to WCF 30.3-30.4 and Heidelberg Q83-85. Dropped the Baptist confession reference as outside the school's confessional standards and added Belgic Confession 30-31 and WCF 25.6, 30.1, and 31.
